_readme: Run-2 outcome: crashed after ~115k FUN_00668380 calls in ~40s.
Diagnosis via verify_manifest_vas.py:
- 6 of 8 'confirmed' Group-A VAs land MID-FUNCTION in GDI
(they're DirectDraw addresses; the two binaries have
different function layouts and non-uniform deltas).
- Interceptor.attach on a non-prologue address corrupts the
instruction stream around the target — the crash arrives
when normal execution walks through those bytes.
- The 3 that ARE exact GDI function starts (0x00668380,
0x0055EC00, 0x004938D0) do NOT have the identities the
DirectDraw names imply. Run 2 proved 0x00668380 in GDI
is a hot per-frame fn with a non-club first arg, NOT
promotion_install.
Rule: no hook is enabled unless its VA is an EXACT match to a
sub_XXXXXXXX.asm file in D:/cm0102-carve/gdi_carve/functions/
AND its identity has been re-verified in GDI (not just carried
over from DirectDraw archaeology). Run verify_manifest_vas.py
before EVERY capture attempt.
Current config: ALL Group A disabled pending GDI-address
archaeology. Group B stays enabled — those 7 VAs are all
exact GDI function starts sourced from GDI-specific memory
notes (frozen fixture tranche) and were confirmed working in
run 2 (fired sparsely, no crash before Group A blew up).
`va` is the GDI VA. `dd_va_hint` records the DirectDraw
equivalent for cross-reference — the GDI delta is NON-UNIFORM.
Any hook whose only source is a DirectDraw address is labelled
`_DD` in its name and DISABLED. Groups C/D/E/F remain disabled.

A_year_end.description: ALL DISABLED after run-2 diagnosis. The FUN_XXXXXXXX names in memory point at DirectDraw addresses; the GDI binary lays out functions differently. Verifier (verify_manifest_vas.py) showed 6 of these VAs land mid-function in GDI (jump-patch crash risk); 3 are exact matches to real GDI functions but their identities in GDI are NOT the same as in DirectDraw (run 2 proved 0x00668380 in GDI is a hot per-frame function with a non-club first arg, NOT promotion_install). Correct GDI addresses need to be looked up in D:/cm0102-carve/gdi_carve/ per function.

hooks.name: FUN_00668450_shared_driver
hooks.note: C11.3: driver enter now records arg0 raw+int, comp record (id + first 128 bytes), and return address. That lets us identify the specific competition (e.g. runtime ptr 0x6014fb0 in the previous capture) and the immediate caller.

hooks.name: sub_0055F540_schedule_getter
hooks.note: C11.3: schedule_getter enter now records arg0 raw+int, comp record (id + first 128 bytes) if arg0 is a plausible pointer, and the return address on the stack. Enables mid-season regen trigger archaeology.
